questions.q: What does the CommonSecurityLog query show about the 3 AM connection?
options: DeviceAction == "Deny", proving the firewall blocked it
DeviceAction == "Allow", proving the firewall deliberately let it through
No log entry exists for the connection at all
The connection used port 443, not 3389
questions.explain: The log shows the connection was allowed, which redirects the investigation toward why the firewall allowed it.

questions.q: Which rule does the firewall's rule-hit history show matched the connection?
options: A rule with no name, indicating a misconfiguration
A default any-any allow rule
ALLOW-VENDOR-RDP-SUPPORT (FW-0231), the rule built in Lesson 4 for vendor remote support
A rule created that same night by an unknown administrator
questions.explain: The connection matched the existing vendor-support rule from Lesson 4, not a new or unnamed rule.

questions.q: Why does matching the vendor rule reframe the investigation?
options: It proves 198.51.212.77 is definitely malicious
It proves the firewall rule's configured address range -- not the vendor connection itself -- is the thing to check
It proves the alert from Lesson 8 was a false positive and can be closed
It proves the correlation rule from Lesson 5 is broken
questions.explain: The firewall only checks whether a source IP falls inside a rule's configured range, so a match means the range itself is the thing to examine.

questions.q: What does the lesson explicitly say NOT to do yet?
options: Query CommonSecurityLog for the source IP and port
Check the firewall's rule-hit history for a match
Disable the vendor support rule outright or assume the IP is confirmed malicious
Note the rule ID for later reference
questions.explain: Neither fact is confirmed yet, and disabling the rule would break a legitimate vendor connection without a plan.

questions.q: What business need does the ALLOW-VENDOR-RDP-SUPPORT rule legitimately serve?
options: Letting any internet host reach the jump host
Letting Hartwell's metering-support vendor reach the jump host for scheduled maintenance
Letting employees work from home over RDP
Letting the correlation rule from Lesson 5 query the firewall directly
questions.explain: The rule exists for a real, reasonable business purpose -- vendor remote support -- which is why disabling it outright isn't the right first move.
